record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the one-dimensional lubrication approximation of a thin neck in a Hele-Shaw cell, with neck thickness h satisfying the reduced local model h_t + (h h_zzz)_z = 0, can one prove the spatial regularity required for the approximation to remain valid as a singularity forms, specifically that h has at least a bounded first spatial derivative up to breakup?

evidence.quote: To respect the approximation, we require the solution to have at least a bounded first derivative as as singularity forms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional lubrication approximation describing the thickness h(z,t) > 0 of a thin neck of fluid in a Hele-Shaw cell, governed by the fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation
  h_t + (h · h_{zzz})_z = 0,
for z in a bounded interval (say [-1,1]) with suitable boundary conditions enforcing a pressure jump, and smooth positive initial data h(·,0). It is known (and expected) that for sufficiently large pressure jump such solutions pinch off, i.e. there exists a finite or infinite time T* with inf h(z,t) → 0 as t → T*.

Prove that, for the approximation to remain self-consistent, the spatial regularity of h is preserved up to the breakup time; specifically, show that the first spatial derivative h_z remains uniformly bounded on the time interval [0, T*), i.e.
  sup_{t ∈ [0, T*)} ‖h_z(·,t)‖_{L^∞} < ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: Constantin, Elgindi, Nguyen, and Vicol (2018, Comm. Math. Phys.) rigorously studied this Hele-Shaw lubrication model h_t + (h h_zzz)_z = 0, proving that smooth positive initial data lead to pinch-off (inf h → 0) in finite or infinite time for sufficiently large pressure jump, and establishing regularity results up to pinch-off. This addresses the qualitative regularity question, though whether the precise bound ‖h_z‖_∞ < ∞ up to the singular time is fully established in all regimes is not entirely clear from public abstracts; the problem appears to be at least partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: On Singularity Formation in a Hele-Shaw Model
status_evidence.snippet: Starting from smooth and positive h, as long as h>0 no singularity arises. For pressure jump P>2 and any smooth positive initial datum, the solution pinches off in finite or infinite time.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous results on regularity and pinch-off for h_t + (h h_zzz)_z = 0 were proven by Constantin–Elgindi–Nguyen–Vicol (2018).

status_evidence.title: [1708.08490] On singularity formation in a Hele-Shaw model
status_evidence.snippet: On singularity formation in a Hele-Shaw model — Constantin, Elgindi, Nguyen, Vicol.
status_evidence.claim: arXiv preprint addressing singularity formation in the same Hele-Shaw lubrication model.
